sections.title: Form and nomenclature
sections.text: A climbing epiphytic or rock-dwelling cactus from Central America. The catalogue name Hylocereus costaricensis is now treated by Kew as Selenicereus costaricensis.

sections.title: Stems, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The triangular stems are usually 3–6 cm across and sometimes larger. Large night-blooming flowers reach 20–30 cm. The red, ovoid fruits are about 8–10 × 6–8 cm and have purple flesh.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The ripe fruit pulp is eaten. This does not apply to other parts of the cactus.
